claim: A rental provider or agent cannot ask whether an applicant has taken legal action or had a dispute with a previous rental provider.
review_notes: Supported by the application rules.

claim: If weekly rent is above $900, a rental provider can invite a renter to pay more than one month's rent in advance.
review_notes: The claim is supported by the rent-in-advance rules, although it does not answer the original rental-bidding question.

claim: A Victorian rental property must have a fixed heater in good working order in the main living area.
review_notes: Supported by the minimum heating requirements.

claim: For rental agreements starting from 29 March 2023, the fixed heater in the main living area must be energy efficient.
review_notes: Supported by the energy-efficiency requirement for agreements starting from 29 March 2023.

claim: The completed and signed condition report must be returned within 5 business days of moving in.
review_notes: Supported by the condition report requirements.

claim: If rent is paid weekly, up to 2 weeks rent can be requested in advance.
review_notes: Supported by the weekly rent-in-advance rule.

claim: If rent is paid monthly and weekly rent is $900 or less, up to one month rent can be requested in advance.
review_notes: Supported by the monthly rent-in-advance rule.

claim: If weekly rent is above $900, more than one month's rent can be requested in advance.
review_notes: Supported by the rule for weekly rent above $900.

claim: A rental provider must give at least 90 days notice before a rent increase.
review_notes: The 90-day rent increase notice requirement is supported by the retrieved evidence.

claim: A rental provider who wants to refuse a pet request must apply to VCAT within 14 days.
review_notes: Supported by the pet refusal process.

claim: A rental property must have a fixed heater in good working order in the main living area.
review_notes: Supported by the minimum heating requirements.

claim: A non-working fixed heater is considered a non-urgent repair.
review_notes: The retrieved evidence does not support classifying a non-working fixed heater as a non-urgent repair.

claim: If the rental provider does not respond, the renter can arrange and pay for the repair if it costs no more than $2500.
review_notes: The $2500 self-arranged repair process applies to urgent repairs, but the answer applies it after incorrectly classifying the heater issue as non-urgent.

claim: The renter can use the Notice to rental provider of rented premises form to request reimbursement.
review_notes: The retrieved urgent-repair process supports using the relevant notice form to request reimbursement.

claim: Receipts, invoices or other proof of repairs are needed when requesting reimbursement.
review_notes: The retrieved repair process supports providing receipts, invoices or other evidence of the repair.

claim: A rental provider must use the Notice of rent increase form and provide at least 90 days notice before increasing the rent.
review_notes: Supported by the rent increase notice requirements.

claim: A renter can ask Consumer Affairs Victoria to investigate if they believe a rent increase is too high.
review_notes: Supported by the Consumer Affairs Victoria rent assessment process.

claim: The renter must contact Consumer Affairs Victoria within 30 days of receiving the rent increase notice.
review_notes: Supported by the 30-day assessment deadline.

claim: The renter can use the Request for rental assessment form to request a rent assessment.
review_notes: Supported by the rent assessment process.

claim: A renter can provide evidence when disputing a rental provider's bond claim.
review_notes: Supported by the bond dispute process.

claim: RDRV can review the bond dispute, discuss it with both parties and try to help reach a fair outcome.
review_notes: Supported by the RDRV bond dispute process.

claim: When moving out, the property must be reasonably clean and in the same condition as when the renter moved in, allowing for fair wear and tear.
review_notes: Supported by the moving-out and fair wear and tear requirements.

claim: Pre-existing damage can be used as a reason to dispute responsibility for the damage.
review_notes: The retrieved condition-report and moving-out evidence supports using pre-existing damage when disputing responsibility.

claim: Photos or other documentation can be used as evidence that damage existed before the renter moved in.
review_notes: Photos can be used to document the property's condition.

claim: Rental agreements signed on or after 29 March 2021 can have additional professional cleaning requirements.
review_notes: Supported by the professional cleaning requirements.

claim: A rental provider cannot end a rental agreement without a valid reason, including at the end of a fixed-term agreement.
review_notes: Supported by the rules for ending a rental agreement.

claim: Valid reasons can include the provider or family moving in, major renovations or demolition.
review_notes: Supported by the listed valid reasons for issuing a Notice to vacate.

claim: A rental provider cannot evict a renter for using or intending to use their rental rights.
review_notes: Supported by the protection against eviction for exercising rental rights.
